item.title: ‘Good riddance’… Fans react as Tom Brady officially quits English soccer club Birmingham City
item.description: Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images The Tom Brady era at Birmingham City has come to an end. English soccer club Birmingham City has confirmed that Tom Brady will play no further part in their future. Brady acquired a minority stake in the club through his partnership with Knighthead Capital Management, led by Tom Wagner. He held a role as chairman of the club’s advisory board, and as commercial and brand ambassador. Now it is all over. Birmingham City released a statement, reading: “Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years. “It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.” Tom Brady’s Birmingham City timeline August 2023: Tom Brady joins Birmingham City as minority investor October 2023: Manager John Eustace fired and replaced with Wayne Rooney January 2024: Wayne Rooney sacked after only 15 games May 2024: Birmingham City relegated to League One May 2025: Birmingham City promoted to Championship November 2026: Tom Brady leaves role with Birmingham 1st in the Championship Fans react to Brady departure The timing of Tom Brady’s departure is curious with Birmingham City top of the Championship and hoping to be promoted to the Premier League, after a turbulent three years. However, the reaction of fans to his exit casted doubt on Brady’s role, and whether it would make any difference at all. One fan wrote: “Shame but no real shock. Did his part and now got other stuff going on. We’ve still got Tom Wagner and that’s all that matters.” Another posted: “Good riddance. only came for the documentary, don’t need people like him round our club.” A third added: “It’s a shame but what can we do, unfortunate he had all the NFL to deal with. We move on, not the end of the world.” Other comments included, “What exactly did he do?”, and “Thought he’d reappear now we’re top of the league.” Another message noted: “A statement from himself would have been better.” Brady remains an investor in NFL franchise the Las Vegas Raiders, and continues to commentate on NFL games for FOX. item.title: NFL trade deadline: The Jaguars are all-in; should the 49ers follow suit?
item.description: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers have the best record in the NFL right now, with the Minnesota Vikings playing tonight on Monday Night Football. Trade rumors are swirling, and the team suffered a blow with the loss of defensive tackle Gracen Halton. The trade deadline is tomorrow, and there is plenty of time left to add to the roster. The Jacksonville Jaguars have sent a message to the AFC and the NFL with the acquisitions of safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. It feels like just about any year you can say the NFL is “wide open,” but this season seems to be more open than seasons past. Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch haven’t indicated they are all-in or completely out in public statements. In my opinion, I’d bet the 49ers are working the phones right now. Evaluating the in-house talent and the incoming reinforcements is part of the equation for the 49ers. We do know the 49ers targeted Jauan Jennings in a trade with Minnesota, but that move felt like a depth improvement, given his familiarity with the offense. Should the 49ers take a page from the Jaguars’ playbook? Now, look, teams shouldn’t be reactionary to other teams’ moves or thought processes. It is possible for the 49ers to be fine with what they have. There is the possibility that the 49ers, who have run the ball very well in 2026, will shift their identity in January to a running team that controls the clock and wants their defense to eliminate offenses. You don’t suspect you will be in shootouts in the playoffs, and of course anything is possible. On the flip side, adding firepower is never a bad idea, provided the value of the return and the investment is reasonable. Do the 49ers have confidence in the returns of Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, and De’Zhaun Stribling, potentially with Demarcus Robinson rounding into shape? The pass rush hasn’t flashed as much as you would like, but do the 49ers add a familiar face off the street, Leonard Floyd, anyone? The 49ers have taken swings in the past. Will the 49ers stand pat or bet on the return of CJ West to bolster the defensive tackle depth? Should the 49ers swing on a wide receiver or hope that Jordan Watkins’ development will continue? Calling the Jets about Will McDonald IV isn’t the worst idea. Sound off in the comments: should the 49ers follow Jacksonville’s trade process?

item.title: Why Phillies' interest in Ha-Seong Kim would make for a bad free agent addition
item.description: Why Phillies' interest in Ha-Seong Kim would make for a bad free agent addition originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies have a lot of work to do this offseason to not only fix this roster, fill the new roster holes, and upgrade where necessary, but also to prove to the fans that this is a team worth trusting again. For the Phillies, there are plenty of roster moves worth considering, including adding help to the infield depth with Alec Bohm and Edmundo Sosa both hitting free agency this offseason. According to Jim Salisbury of NBC Sports Philadelphia , they have interest in Ha-Seong Kim to add to their infield. But such an addition would be a bad idea, as Kim doesn't provide anything this Phillies team needs. Phillies' interest in Ha-Seong Kim might be a mistake "According to sources, the Phillies are eyeing that type of player in free agent Ha-Seong Kim," Salisbury reports. The former San Diego Padres , Tampa Bay Rays , and Atlanta Braves infielder previously won a Gold Glove in his career and has had some nice moments. But that's well in the past now. After signing for a one-year, $20 million deal last offseason with the Braves, he suffered a freak injury in Korea that forced him to miss a significant amount of time and derailed his 2026 season. On the year with the Braves, Kim posted a negative 0.7 bWAR across 129 at-bats. He wasn't a good defender, and he hit just .116 with no home runs and a terrible .359 OPS. The Phillies really shouldn't have interest in adding Kim, despite their reported interest in the veteran infielder from Salisbury. MORE : Braves predicted to trade Ronald Acuna Jr. for Phillies' $330M two-time MVP in monster deal Kim doesn't provide much of anything offensively, with his .524 OPS the past two seasons being well below league average. His 47 OPS+ shows that his offensive value was less than half that of the league-average hitter. The Phillies would be better off promoting someone from the minor leagues or taking a chance on a cheaper option than trying to make Kim work. There is a chance that Kim's 2026 season was completely derailed due to his torn tendon in his middle finger, and that a year removed from the injury, he plays at a much higher level. But even if Kim were to dramatically improve, it's unlikely he'd be much more than an average hitter at best. While he could provide decent defensive upside if he returns to form there, his overall value is worth questioning. It's one thing if the Phillies add Kim as a bench option in a similar role to what Sosa played this past season. But if the Phillies are relying on Kim to be a starter, this interest in Kim might be a mistake. item.title: ‘That’s What You Sign Up For’: Chiefs Kicker Harrison Butker Addresses Brutal Home Crowd Reaction After Another Miss
item.description: Harrison Butker and the Kansas City Chiefs had a great win over the New York Jets. The team won with a score of 35-12, and it was their sixth win of the season. The franchise has a good record in the 2026 NFL season, with only two losses so far. Despite their stable condition in the league, the team still has many issues. One of those is Butker, and the player recently talked about it. Harrison Butker addresses missed field goal Butker has struggled a lot this season, and it also happened in the Week 9 victory against the Jets. With seconds remaining in the first half and the Chiefs leading 14-12, the kicker attempted a 56-yard field goal that sailed wide right. A Jets offsides penalty moved the ball five yards closer, giving him a 51-yard retry, with that kick also being missed wide right. Aug 17, 2024; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker (7) on the sidelines against the Detroit Lions during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-USA TODAY Sports Butker has seven missed field goals through nine weeks, the most in the NFL. His season conversion rate stood at 63.2 percent (12-of-19). Since the start of the 2025 season, he has missed 17 total kicks (12 field goals and five extra points), which is the highest in the league. These have brought him much criticism, with the home crowd booing him in the Jets game. After the game, Butker took direct responsibility for his repeated failures. He said , “I’m booing myself sometimes. People are passionate, the fans are passionate. They want to win games. They want me to make kicks. I want to make kicks. It’s part of it. That’s what you sign up for and I’ve got to be better.” After the game, head coach Andy Reid also talked about the player. Andy Reid speaks on Harrison Butker issues After the game, Reid was asked about Butker and declined to make an immediate roster decision. He said , “I’m sure I’ll be asked about Butker. I’ll address that as we go throughout the week. I’ll look at everything, and no need to ask. That’ll be the answer that you get. I’m not making any decisions right now today.” The Chiefs had previously signed former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad to create competition. It remains to be seen whether the team will make any changes to the roster. Harrison Butker and the Chiefs will now focus on the next game against the Atlanta Falcons. After more than two years and myriad subliminal disses, Brandon Aiyuk is on the cusp of returning to the field. The NFL formally reinstated the disgruntled wideout, giving the 49ers two weeks to figure out his future. Aiyuk has long been linked with a move out of town. The 28-year-old flirted with the idea of leaving for much of the past two seasons, much to team officials' chagrin. He should have his chance to do so in the coming few weeks, although he might not have the pick of the litter of choices after burning bridges with San Francisco's front office. With that, here's what we know about Aiyuk's reinstatement, including what's next for the soon-to-be former 49ers pass-catcher. LIVE: Updates on Jonathan Taylor, Derrick Henry and more trade rumors What's next for Brandon Aiyuk? Naturally, some might believe Aiyuk's reinstatement might offer a pathway for the 49ers to bring him back into the fold. The likelihood of that happening is low, however. Both Aiyuk and San Francisco appear content with the impending split — the former didn't report to the 49ers' offseason program or training camp, landing on the left-team list while the latter voided $27 million in guarantees directed towards the wideout. The league informed Aiyuk that he'd have to pay back $13 million of restitution to his employers to be reinstated. That sum, the total of bonus money issued to Aiyuk after signing his deal, was seen as a major snag in his pursuit to get back on the field. Aiyuk and agent Drew Rosenhaus met with San Francisco personnel on Friday in the hopes of working towards a resolution. Monday's announcement suggests that pursuit was successful. The league granted the Niners a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero. Aiyuk will not start counting towards San Francisco's 53-man active roster list until Week 12, giving the team two weeks to orchestrate a move to get him out of town. The Niners could try to float Aiyuk as a low-cost trade chip to wide receiver-needy teams. The market for the former second-team All-Pro pass-catcher remains unknown — Aiyuk hasn't caught a ball since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee in Oct. 2024. In the event they can't find a suitor willing to part ways with draft capital to acquire Aiyuk's services, one would have to expect the 49ers to waive him. General manager John Lynch proclaimed that Aiyuk had played his last snap with San Francisco in January, while head coach Kyle Shanahan bluntly denied that the team would consider adding Aiyuk to its ranks amid a series of injuries to other wideouts in September. item.description: Aryna Sabalenka kept her Indian Wells win streak alive Monday, defeating Karolina Muchova, 7-6(2), 7-5 in the WTA Finals round robin. The match was the first for both players this week and was the first match of Day 2 of the event that runs until Sunday. The event is being held in Indian Wells this year, after being held the two previous years in Riyadh, and includes the top-eight ranked women in the world and the top-ranked doubles teams. Sabalenka is the top seed in the draw after top-ranked Elena Rybakina withdrew Saturday due to what the WTA described as a "viral illness." The Belarus tennis star won the BNP Paribas Open title here in March and her win streak now extends to seven matches. Three of those wins came against top 10 players, including Monday's. Sabalenka overcame some early trouble to win the match, too. She lost her serve twice in the opening set, only to get back on serve both times. Muchova, of Czechia, went up a break a second time at 5-4 and had a chance to serve for the set. But Sabalenka didn't go quietly. She won the first two points of the 10th game and easily avoided losing the set by winning the game. In the next game, with the score tied, 5-5, Sabalanka became the second woman this year to earn her 300th ace of the season. Only Rybakina has recorded more. Sabalenka took back control of the set by holding serve and taking the 6-5 lead. After Muchova held serve to even the score, Sabalenka took the early lead in the tiebreak and never trailed. She then carried that momentum into the second set and held off a late push by Muchova to force another tiebreak as the nearly packed Stadium 2 roared inside the Indian Wells Tennis Garden.
